calls.ret: An array of lowercase layer names, in arbitrary order.

calls.doc: Declarative convergence: diffs the declared {present=, absent=} set against what's actually loaded and issues only the minimal add/remove, fixing drift instead of blindly re-applying everything.
Restores exactly to the recorded baseline (diffing current state against it, not a tracked delta), so it's correct even if something else changed layers mid-mode, then un-gates saves.
True while a layers mode is open.
Whether one named dynamic layer is loaded right now. Case-insensitive - the name is lowercased before the lookup.
Unloads layer(s); same STATIC-layer refusal as add.

The set of dynamic layers that were loaded at the moment Ess.Layers.begin ran - the baseline that finishing the mode restores back to. Compare it against Ess.Layers.current to see what a mode has changed.
calls.ret: An array of lowercase layer names, or an empty array when no mode is open.

calls.doc: Remove-then-add, sequenced so the removal's callback chains into the add - the standard mission idiom for swapping layer sets.

namespaces.name: Ess.Loop
namespaces.doc: The one shared reload-safe heartbeat

calls.doc: Whether a loop is currently registered under that id. Check it before Ess.Loop.start when you only want to confirm a loop is armed - start() reschedules a running loop rather than leaving it alone, so an unconditional call keeps pushing the next tick back.
the shape a dashboard/monitor wants to poll on an interval and just render.
calls.ret: { {id=, interval=, ticks=, lastDuration=, avgDuration=, lastError=}, ... }, sorted by id

calls.doc: Registers (or replaces) a self-rescheduling loop under id; tickFn() runs every interval seconds (default 1), returning true/truthy to keep going or false/nil to auto-stop. Calling again with the same id safely supersedes any previous loop under it; a tick that errors is pcall-caught, logged, and treated as stop.
calls.gotcha: Calling start() again with the SAME id supersedes the previous loop instead of stacking a second one -- that's what makes it safe to call unconditionally from the top of a re-run OnKey script. Hand-rolled self-rescheduling Event timers do NOT do this and leak a whole extra loop on every keypress.

calls.doc: safe to hold onto and print without it changing under you.
calls.ret: { interval, ticks, lastDuration, avgDuration, lastError } | nil

calls.doc: Cancels a running loop early. Its next scheduled tick sees it's gone and quietly does not reschedule — no error.

namespaces.name: Ess.Mark
namespaces.doc: .object(guid, {radar=, pda=, world=, disc=, kind=, rgb=, radius=, discAlpha=, size=, dist=}), .zone(x,y,z,r, {world=, radar=, pda=, icon=, kind=, rgb=, discAlpha=, size=, dist=}), .clear(handle) — every surface (radar / PDA / ground ring / floating icon) is an independent opt, so one call covers any combination

calls.doc: Tears down every marker surface present in a handle, plus the zone's anchor prop if it has one. Safe to call on a partial handle — any missing/nil field is simply skipped.

Marks an existing object's uGuid across whichever surfaces opts enable (radar/pda/world/disc; radar, pda, and world default to true). Returns a compound handle table {uGuid, radarName?, pdaName?, worldHandle?, discHandle?} covering only the surfaces actually drawn.

Marks a bare world point by first spawning an invisible TinyGeometry anchor at (x,y,z) via Ess.Object.spawn, then marking that anchor. Returns nil if the anchor fails to spawn; the returned handle owns the anchor, so Ess.Mark.clear removes the anchor prop too.

namespaces.name: Ess.Math
namespaces.doc: Geometry/number helpers in the engine's yaw convention

calls.doc: The yaw that faces from (fromX,fromZ) toward (toX,toZ), in the engine's own convention (calibrated against Ess.Object.spawnAhead). Returns 0 if the two points coincide.
calls.gotcha: Exact inverse of Ess.Math.pointAhead -- if the yaw convention ever needs revisiting the two MUST be changed as a pair. Verify facing east/west; the error is invisible at yaw 0/180.

calls.doc: Moves cur toward target by at most maxStep — a frame-rate-independent ease when maxStep = speed * dt.
Ess.Math.lerp(a, b, t) -> n            Ess.Math.sign(v) -> -1|0|1
Clamps to the unit range [0, 1] — the common case for a lerp/ease parameter.
Horizontal (X/Z-plane) distance between two points, ignoring height.
dist2D without the sqrt — use when you only need to compare distances ("which is closer").

calls.sig: Ess.Math.dist3D(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)
calls.doc: Straight-line distance between two world points, height (Y) included. Use Ess.Math.dist2D instead when height should be ignored, which is usually what you want for ground units.

calls.sig: Ess.Math.dist3DSq(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)
calls.doc: The squared 3D distance between two points, skipping the square root. Use it when you only ever compare distances - "which is closer", "is it inside the radius".
calls.gotcha: The result is in squared units, so a radius check must compare against r*r, not r. Ess.Math.within3D does that for you.

calls.doc: Blends between a and b by t: 0 gives a, 1 gives b, 0.5 the midpoint. The workhorse for easing a value over time - a fade amount, a camera FOV, a bar fill.
calls.gotcha: t is not clamped, so a value outside 0..1 extrapolates past the endpoints instead of stopping there.

calls.doc: Interpolates angle a -> b (degrees) the shortest way, so 350 -> 10 eases +20 through zero rather than -340 the long way. t is in [0, 1]; result normalized to [-180, 180) — the correct lerp for a turning yaw.
Normalizes an angle so a difference of two yaws reads as the shortest turn (350 and 10 differ by 20, not 340). Handy for facing checks and smooth turn easing.

The point dist units in front of (x, z) when facing yawDeg — exactly Ess.Object.spawnAhead's projection, exposed for reuse (placing something ahead of an NPC, aiming a dolly, offsetting a marker). Y is unchanged.
calls.gotcha: Forward for a yaw is (+sin, +cos) in (x,z). The mirrored (-sin) convention this used to have is INVISIBLE at yaw 0/180 and MAXIMAL at +-90, so always calibrate facing EAST or WEST -- an earlier calibration done facing north "passed" and let the bug survive for months.

calls.doc: Linearly rescales v from [inLo, inHi] onto [outLo, outHi]. A degenerate input range (inLo == inHi) returns outLo instead of dividing by zero; does not clamp the output, so an out-of-range v extrapolates past [outLo, outHi].
-- a local (right,forward) offset -> world
Rounds v to the nearest value; decimals defaults to 0 (nearest integer).
Reduces a number to just its direction, discarding magnitude. Handy for turning a difference into a step direction.
calls.ret: 1 when positive, -1 when negative, 0 when exactly zero.

calls.doc: Eases a 0..1 t to 0..1 with zero slope at both ends (3t² - 2t³), clamping t first. Feed it to lerp for an ease-in-out.
Is the second point within radius r of the first, on the ground plane? A named dx*dx + dz*dz <= r*r test with no sqrt — the check every proximity trigger/"reached the zone" poll open-codes.

calls.sig: Ess.Math.within3D(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2, r)
calls.doc: Tests whether two world points are within r of each other in full 3D, height included. Built on the squared distance, so there is no square root in the hot path.
Wraps v into the half-open range [lo, hi) — for keeping an index, angle, or cursor in-band. hi <= lo returns lo.

namespaces.name: Ess.Net
namespaces.doc: Co-op data sync (native port of ModNet)

calls.doc: Reads a synced value from the default "_" namespace - the partner to Ess.Net.Set.
calls.ret: The value, or nil when the key has never been set.

calls.doc: Whether this machine owns the simulation: true in single-player, and true on the co-op host. The check to gate spawning, scoring and mission logic on so it runs exactly once across the session.
Whether a live co-op session is running right now.
calls.gotcha: The underlying engine flag comes back as a boolean on some paths and as 1/0 on others; the wrapper normalizes both, which is exactly why you should not read the native directly.

calls.doc: Whether this machine is the host of a live co-op session.
calls.gotcha: FALSE in single-player, because it requires a co-op session first. For the "should I run the simulation" question use Ess.Net.IsAuthority, which also answers true for solo play.

calls.doc: This machine's own player id in the session, used as the `sender` value on every received message.
Registers a receiver for channel name; fn(sender, value) is invoked when a message arrives on that channel (sender is the 0/1 player id).

Registers a receiver for a raw numeric channel: fn(sender, nums) fires with the peer's player id and the number array exactly as it was sent, with no serialization in between. Pair it with Ess.Net.SendRaw on the same channel name.
calls.gotcha: One handler per channel - registering the same name again REPLACES the previous handler rather than adding to a list. Channel names are hashed to 16 bits, so two different names can in principle collide onto the same channel.

calls.doc: Serializes value (string/number/bool/nil/nested table) and sends it chunked over the wire on channel name. reliable defaults to true; pass false for an unreliable send.

Sends an array of plain numbers on a channel to the co-op peer, skipping serialization entirely - the expert path when you already have numeric data and want the smallest possible packet. Pass reliable=false for fire-and-forget.
calls.gotcha: In co-op nothing goes out until the peer's ready handshake has completed: the send is silently DROPPED, not queued. Numbers must be 24-bit safe, and a payload larger than the per-packet slots is split into several packets and reassembled on the far side.

calls.doc: Writes a synced value in the default "_" namespace - the shorthand for Ess.Net.setv when you only need one shared bucket.
calls.gotcha: Broadcasts on every call, exactly like Ess.Net.setv.

calls.doc: Returns a plain-looking table for a namespace whose reads and writes route through the synced store: `S.score = 100` broadcasts, and reading S.score on either machine returns the latest value. The simplest layer of Ess.Net - no channels, no callbacks.
calls.gotcha: It is a proxy with no real contents, so pairs, ipairs and # all see an empty table. Values are stored at write time, so mutating a nested table in place never syncs - reassign the whole field instead.
calls.ret: A proxy table backed by the synced store.

calls.doc: Registers a local value to be polled and pushed to the peer on the heartbeat: getter() is called every Ess.Net.HB seconds and the result synced under `key` in namespace `ns` (default "_"). The right tool for a value that changes constantly, such as health, where broadcasting each change would flood the wire.
calls.gotcha: Idempotent - calling again with the same ns and key just swaps the getter, which is what makes it safe to re-run on a reload. There is no untrack: once registered, a key stays on the watch list for the rest of the session.

calls.doc: Reads the current synced value for a key in a namespace, whether it was set locally or arrived from the peer.
calls.ret: The value, or nil when that namespace/key has never been set.

calls.doc: Wraps an existing engine callback so your handler claims only the calls it recognises: isMinePredicate(...) decides, onMine(...) handles those, and everything else falls through to the original untouched. This is the generalized recipe Ess.Net's own wire protocol uses to share the game's faction-event channel without breaking the game's own traffic.
calls.gotcha: Both callbacks run inside pcall and their errors are swallowed, so a throwing predicate is treated as "not mine" and quietly hands the call on. Only the first four return values of the original are forwarded.
calls.ret: Whatever Ess.Override.wrap returns - false when the target is not a table, the named field is not a function, or it is already Ess-wrapped.

calls.doc: Writes a value into a synced namespace, bumps its version number and immediately broadcasts it to the peer. Conflicts resolve last-writer-wins by version.
calls.gotcha: Every single write sends a packet, so do not call it on a per-frame tick - use Ess.Net.Track for a value that changes constantly. Keys written by both machines converge unpredictably; keep each key single-writer or host-authoritative.

namespaces.name: Ess.Object
namespaces.doc: The everyday object-manipulation namespace

calls.doc: Attaches a text label to an object. Labels are the engine's own free-form tagging mechanism - a way to stamp "mine" on a spawned unit so later code can recognise it.
calls.gotcha: Silent on failure, and nothing is returned.

calls.doc: Whether an object is still alive - the check to poll for "has the target died yet".
calls.gotcha: false covers both "dead" and "the engine call failed", so it cannot distinguish a corpse from a bad guid. Combine with Ess.Object.valid when you need to tell them apart. The native returns 1/0 here rather than a boolean; the wrapper normalizes it.

calls.doc: deal damage (kills if it would drop <= 0)
Freezes one object out of the physics simulation - useful for pinning a prop in place for a cutscene or stopping a spawned vehicle from rolling away.
calls.gotcha: Silent on failure, and nothing is returned.

calls.doc: Returns the localized, human-readable name (Object.GetLocalizedName) for HUD/labels — distinct from Ess.Name(guid), which is the guid's hash string.

Collapses Object.GetDistanceFrom's two forms — object-to-object (uGuidA, uGuidB, bIgnoreY) and object-to-coordinates (uGuidA, x, y, z, bIgnoreY) — into one call, dispatching on whether the 2nd argument is a number.
Turns the engine's physics simulation back on for one object, so it falls, collides and reacts to impulses again.
calls.gotcha: Silent on failure, and nothing is returned.

calls.doc: Like faceToward, but faces another object's current position rather than a fixed point.
Turns the object to face a world point using ground-plane yaw (y is accepted for call convenience but unused). Uses Ess.Math.angleTo so the convention matches the engine's own.
Checks whether an object carries a free-form string tag (labels like "PMC"/"Disposable"/"garage" that the engine and other scripts read).
The confirmed "heal to full" idiom: Object.SetHealth(uGuid, Object.GetMaxHealth(uGuid)).
Ess.Object.setHealth(uGuid, n)
Ess.Object.snapToGround(uGuid, nOffset) -> ok

Wraps Object.ApplyImpulse, the confirmed launch/knock-around primitive; real call sites scale the impulse by the object's mass since heavier things need a bigger push. bLocal defaults to true (impulse in the object's own space). This is the bare call — see Ess.Impulse for mass-scaling + directional + preset helpers.
the missing getter for setInvincible.

Destroys the object, leaving a corpse/wreck (distinct from remove, which deletes outright). Confirmed not instantaneous: alive(uGuid) still reads true in the same tick as the kill and flips to false a moment later — poll alive() over a couple ticks rather than checking immediately after.
full 3D local->world (incl. pitch/roll -- use over Ess.Math.rotateOffset when the object may be tilted)
Ess.Object.heal(uGuid)   (set-to-GetMaxHealth)

Live discovery: Object.IsPlayerControlled actually returns the controlling player's guid (userdata), not a plain boolean, so a naive truthy() check would misreport the real player as not controlled. This wrapper instead checks "returned a real value" (v ~= nil and v ~= false and v ~= 0).

Watches a character for entering/exiting a vehicle by polling Vehicle.GetFromRider on a heartbeat (default 0.5s), firing onChange(uVehicleOrNil, uPrevVehicleOrNil) on the nil<->guid transition. Polls rather than hooking because there's no native "entered a vehicle" event for an unknown target vehicle. Returns a stop() function to end the watch early.
pcall-wrapped Object.GetPosition — the native throws on an invalid/dead guid, this returns nil instead.
Deletes an object from the world outright - the counterpart to Ess.Object.spawn, and how mission cleanup gets rid of everything it spawned.
calls.gotcha: Nothing is returned, and removing an already-gone guid is a silent no-op, which is what makes double cleanup safe.

calls.doc: Strips a previously attached text label from an object. The suffix to Ess.Object.addLabel.
calls.gotcha: Silent on failure, and removing a label that was never there is indistinguishable from success.

calls.doc: nDelay is an optional, confirmed second argument passed through to Object.Revive.
Sets an object's health outright, without any damage event. Use it to top a unit back up or to soften something before a scripted kill.
calls.gotcha: Silent on failure - an invalid guid is a no-op with no return value to check.

calls.doc: sReason is mandatory here (unlike the native, which allows omitting it) — every real call site tags a reason ("Survival"/"Hijack"/"HQ") so a toggle can always be attributed. An invalid/missing reason logs a warning and falls back to "Ess" rather than failing.

Teleports an object. Confirmed unreliable on freshly-spawned/AI humans (streaming/physics can snap them back) — use Ess.Player.teleport for the player or Ess.Vehicle.followGhost for a dynamic follow. Solid for props/vehicles and for placing a just-spawned object before it streams in.
Shows or hides an object's model without removing it from the world - the object still exists, collides and can be scripted. Anything truthy is coerced to a real boolean before the call.
calls.gotcha: Silent on failure, and nothing is returned.

calls.doc: Turns an object to face a compass bearing in degrees. Pair it with Ess.Math.angleTo to aim one object at another.
calls.gotcha: Returns nothing and never reports failure - a dead or invalid guid just does nothing. Turn Ess.DEBUG on to hear about the swallowed error.

calls.doc: model bounding-box extents (takes a GUID, not a name)
drop (or lift) the object so it sits on the terrain, optionally hovering nOffset units above it.

Creates a new object from a template name at a world position, optionally turned to face `yaw`. The one CREATE verb in Ess.Object - everything else in the namespace drives an object that already exists.
calls.gotcha: A blank or whitespace-only template hard-CRASHES the engine and pcall cannot catch a native crash, which is why the string is validated before the call rather than wrapped in one. Never route around this wrapper by calling Pg.Spawn directly with an unvalidated name.
calls.ret: The new object's guid, or nil when the template was blank or the spawn failed (both cases log).

calls.doc: Spawns sTemplate nDist units (default 18) in front of player i (default local), nHeight units up (default 0 — raise it for aircraft/a midair drop), facing the same way the player faces. Hides the yaw-to-sin/cos trig via Ess.Math.pointAhead.
calls.gotcha: "In front of me" means in front of the BODY, because Object.GetYaw on a character is chest orientation, not view direction -- stand still, swing the mouse, and the spawn still lands where your torso points. Pass tOpts.useView = true for view-relative placement.

calls.doc: How fast an object is currently moving, as a single scalar. One native call plus a square root.
calls.gotcha: For a plain threshold test ("is it moving faster than X") use Ess.Object.speedSq against X*X instead - it skips the square root.
calls.ret: The speed, or nil when the velocity could not be read (dead or invalid guid).

calls.doc: scalar speed. One native call (Object.GetVelocitySquared) + a sqrt.
Whether a guid still refers to a real object at all. Broader than Ess.Object.alive - a corpse is still a valid object.
calls.gotcha: As with alive, a false can also mean the engine call itself threw. The native returns 1/0 and the wrapper normalizes it.

calls.doc: Unifies 4 overlapping entry points across 2 namespaces (Object.InSeat/InVehicle, Player.GetControlledObject, Vehicle.GetFromRider) into the confirmed idiom Vehicle.GetFromRider(char) — works for driver or passenger.
Ess.Object.speed(uGuid) -> n | nil  (.speedSq no-sqrt)
Wraps Object.IsVisible, a real boolean-returning native here — distinct from the FlashWidget GetVisible footgun documented elsewhere in Ess.
Reads an object's yaw. Whether the unit is degrees or radians is unconfirmed on this engine (sample scripts disagree) — reading then writing back is self-consistent regardless.

namespaces.name: Ess.Objective
namespaces.doc: A single counted goal on the HUD objective line (state, no Contract)

calls.doc: Creates a counted goal that renders on the HUD objective line as "Collect intel   3/5" and fires onComplete once the count reaches the target. The middle ground between a bare Ess.Hud.objective text line and a whole Ess.Contract. opts takes id, label, target (default 1), slot (default 1), show, onComplete, onProgress and onFail.
calls.gotcha: Passing an `id` that is already live silently CANCELS the previous objective under that id. That is what makes an OnKey script safe to re-run, but it also means two unrelated goals must never share an id.

namespaces.name: Ess.On
namespaces.doc: Intent-named REACTIVE hooks (respond to the world)

calls.doc: death(guid, fn) -> stop(). A real Event.ObjectDeath hook (not a poll) that fires fn() once when the object dies; fn takes no arguments. If guid is falsy, returns a no-op stop() immediately instead of erroring.

calls.sig: Ess.On.enterArea(x, y, z, r, fn, i)
calls.doc: enterArea(x,y,z,r, fn [,i]) -> stop(). Polls every 0.25s; fires once when player i (default 0) comes within horizontal radius r of (x,z) — y is not part of the distance check. Calls fn(px, y, pz) where y is the value you armed it with, not a measured height, then stops itself.

calls.sig: Ess.On.exitArea(x, y, z, r, fn, i)
calls.doc: exitArea(x,y,z,r, fn [,i]) -> stop(). Polls every 0.25s; only counts as 'leaving' after the player has actually been inside the radius first, so arming while already outside won't fire on the next tick. Fires fn(px, y, pz) once, then stops.

healthBelow(guid, pct, fn) -> stop(). Polls every 0.4s. The baseline is NOT max health — it's whatever Ess.Object.health(guid) first reads back when the hook arms, captured once. Fires fn(hp) the first time hp <= base * (pct/100) (pct defaults to 50), then stops; arming against an already-damaged target means the percentage is relative to health at arm time, not true max.

calls.sig: Ess.On.insideArea(x, y, z, r, fn, i)
calls.doc: insideArea(x,y,z,r, fn [,i]) -> stop(). Polls every 0.25s and calls fn(px, y, pz) on every tick the player is inside the radius (a live zone callback), doing nothing on ticks they're outside. Never auto-stops — call the returned stop() yourself.
fn(uGuid) ONCE per world-labeled object as it streams in near player i (the ObjectFilter + Event.ObjectProximity discovery idiom)

playerHurt(fn [,i]) -> stop(). Polls every 0.2s against player i's (default 0) character health, calling fn(newHp, lost) any tick health is lower than the previous tick's reading (lost is the delta). Keeps running until you call stop().

tick(interval, fn) -> stop(). A named, reload-safe Ess.Loop.start(id, interval or 1, fn) under an auto-generated id, so multiple Ess.On.tick hooks never collide with each other or with Ess.Loop ids you manage yourself. fn() runs every interval seconds (default 1), its return value is ignored, and the loop keeps going until stop().

vehicle(fn [,i]) -> stop(). A thin pass-through: resolves player i's character via Ess.Player.character(i or 0), then returns Ess.Object.pollVehicleChange(char, fn) directly. Returns a no-op stop() if there's no character.

namespaces.name: Ess.Override
namespaces.doc: Change engine logic without the tail-call crash

calls.doc: Appends each entry in the data list onto the existing table at t[key], creating t[key] fresh only if it doesn't exist yet, and never replacing an existing table object there. Prefer this over wrap() when the thing you're modding is data a live table already holds — since tables are references, every existing reader of t[key] sees the appended entries immediately with no cache/refresh needed. Refuses (logs + returns false) if t isn't a table.

Replaces target[name] with newFn in a crash-proof way, avoiding the tail-call bug that breaks the engine's getfenv-based module system. newFn is called as newFn(callOriginal, ...), where callOriginal is a closure that safely invokes the real original — newFn never touches the original function directly. Refuses (logs + returns false) if target isn't a table, target[name] isn't a function, or that target/name pair has already been wrapped.
calls.gotcha: NEVER write `return fOriginal(...)` in a wrapper -- that compiles to a Lua TAIL CALL, and this engine's getfenv(n)-based module system throws "no function environment for tail call at level 2" from deep inside the ENGINE's own code, not your mod. Capture the original, call it as a plain statement, return its results on a separate line; this wrapper makes the crashing shape structurally unavailable.

namespaces.name: Ess.Player
namespaces.doc: Player/character identity without the 8-getter sprawl

calls.doc: Resolves a player index straight to Player.GetCamera(slot) in one call.

Returns the player's character guid. `i=0`/nil is the local character (single-player-safe); `i=1` is the co-op secondary character and reliably returns nil outside co-op rather than being coerced into something odd.
Adds cash via MrxPmc.AddCashQty(n, false, "[Ess]") — never Player.SetCash/AddCash, which are confirmed to silently skip the HUD refresh. No player-index argument; always this machine's own wallet.
Adds fuel via MrxPmc.AddFuelQty(n).

Returns the vehicle the player is currently in (driver or passenger), nil on foot — just Ess.Object.vehicleOf on the player's character. Written and internally consistent but not yet confirmed via live testing.
The complement of inVehicle: true exactly when inVehicle(i) returns nil. Same (not yet live-confirmed) status as inVehicle.

One-stop "where is this player, facing which way": returns x, y, z, yaw, character guid, player-slot guid. yaw defaults to 0 if unreadable; x/y/z are nil if there's no character (e.g. i=1 outside co-op).
calls.ret: x, y, z, yaw, uChar, uPlayerSlot

calls.doc: Clears every currently-active out-of-bounds volume for every connected player at once. Only clears what's active right now — doesn't disable the boundary system, so a later mission/area transition can add a new one.
Controller haptic feedback via Pg.Rumble. fLength defaults to 0.2 (real call sites use ~0.15s).

Freezes (false) or restores (true) gameplay input via Player.SetInputEnabled. Confirmed to leave the keyboard-event stream Lua UI reads (Loader.PopKeyEvents) intact, so a chat box can still type while the world is frozen.

Returns the player-slot guid (distinct from the character guid) that Camera.* and some Ai.* calls want. Note: unlike character(1), slot(1) returns a real, non-nil guid even in single-player, so it is NOT a valid co-op check.
calls.gotcha: Ess.Player.slot(1) returns a real, distinct, non-nil guid even in SINGLE-PLAYER -- do not use it as an "are we in co-op" check, it will false-positive. Use Ess.Player.character(1) ~= nil for that.

calls.doc: Wraps Player.GetTargetUnderReticle but reorders the return so the guid comes first (matching Ess.Player convention) instead of the native's coordinates-first, guid-last order.

Warps all connected heroes to one spot (co-op safe) via the confirmed MrxUtil.TeleportHeroesToLocations idiom, deliberately not raw Object.SetPosition (unreliable on characters). onDone fires once the warp completes. Caution: teleporting out of an interior cell unloads it and drops the player onto open-world terrain instead of round-tripping back to the interior coordinate.

The bearing the player is LOOKING along, worked out from whatever the reticle is aimed at - as opposed to the chest/body yaw that Ess.Player.pose returns as its 4th value. Stand still and swing the mouse and these two diverge, so this is the one that matches what the player perceives as "in front of me".
calls.gotcha: Aiming at open sky, or at something closer than 3 units, silently falls back to the body yaw and returns false as the second value. You always get a usable yaw, so branch on that flag if the difference matters to you.
calls.ret: yaw in degrees plus a boolean that is true when the bearing came from a real reticle hit; nil, false when the player has no character.

namespaces.name: Ess.Points
namespaces.doc: Arena spawn-point selection

calls.doc: Splits a spawn-point list into infantry/vehicle/heli tiers by radius (r<=5 infantry, r<=15 vehicle, r>15 heli). If no point qualifies for infantry, .inf falls back to the full input list instead of being empty.

Nearest-first point selection around (refX, refZ), scored by squared horizontal distance only (Y ignored). Three-tier fallback so it's never empty: points within [opts.minDist, opts.maxDist] (default 18/80) capped at opts.maxCount (default 24); if fewer than 4 match, drop the maxDist ceiling; if still zero, return every point unfiltered.

namespaces.name: Ess.Probe
namespaces.doc: Nearby-object collection, one dispatcher

calls.doc: EVERY object matching a template/object name (Ess.Guid returns only one; this is the multi-instance form)

Optional opts: ammo (default "Gunship Shell"), owner (faction name for damage/kill attribution). This is the primitive artillery repeatedly calls; the other Support functions compose different natives directly instead.

namespaces.name: Ess.Table
namespaces.doc: Dense-array repair + collection helpers

calls.doc: Rebuilds a numeric array densely, mutating t in place (and returning it). Fixes the real bug where t[#t] = nil leaves a nil hole that desyncs #/ipairs/table.insert; non-numeric keys are left untouched.
calls.gotcha: Rebuilds a numeric array densely because a nil hole desyncs `#t` from ipairs -- ipairs stops at the first gap while # may report a larger length, so data silently disappears instead of erroring.

calls.doc: Scans a whole table for a value equal to `val`. Uses pairs, so values stored under string keys are searched too.
Duplicates a table one level deep, copying every key from the source (pairs, so map keys come along too).
calls.gotcha: Shallow. Nested tables are shared with the original, not cloned, so mutating a sub-table changes both copies.
calls.ret: A new table with the same keys and values.

calls.doc: Counts every entry in a table, including the string keys that `#t` cannot see. Reach for it whenever a table is used as a set or a map rather than a list.
Builds a new array holding only the array elements for which fn(value, index) returns truthy.
calls.ret: A new, densely packed array - dropped elements leave no holes, so #result is always accurate.

calls.doc: Returns the first array element for which fn(value, index) is truthy, together with where it was found. Use it when you want the matching item itself rather than a yes/no.
calls.ret: value, index - or nil when nothing matches.

calls.doc: Finds where a value sits in the array part of a table.
calls.gotcha: Walks only the array part (ipairs), so a value stored under a string key is never found. Use Ess.Table.contains for a whole-table search.
calls.ret: The 1-based index of the first match, or nil when the value is not there.

calls.doc: Reports whether a table holds nothing at all, array part or map part. Cheaper than counting because it only asks for the first key.
Every key in t, array or not, order unspecified.
Builds a new array by running fn(value, index) over each element of the array part and keeping the result. The source table is left untouched.
calls.ret: A new array with one entry per array element of the source.

calls.doc: Copies src's keys onto dst, with src winning on any collision. The usual way to layer caller-supplied options over a table of defaults.
calls.gotcha: Mutates dst in place - the only non-pure helper in this group - and copies only one level deep. A nil src is treated as an empty table rather than an error.
calls.ret: dst itself, so the call can be chained.

calls.doc: Folds the array part down to a single value: the accumulator starts at init and becomes fn(acc, value, index) for each element. Use it to sum, find a maximum, or build a string from a list.
calls.ret: The final accumulator - or init unchanged when the array part is empty.

calls.doc: Builds a new array with the order of the array part flipped end for end. The source is left alone.
calls.ret: A new array of the same length, reversed.

calls.doc: Extracts elements i through j of the array part, 1-based and inclusive, into a new array. i defaults to 1 and j to #t, and both are clamped to the real bounds.
calls.ret: A new array of the selected elements (empty if the range collapses).

calls.doc: Collects every value in a table into a new array, walking the whole table with pairs so map-style string keys are included, not just the array part.
calls.gotcha: pairs has no defined order, so the result's ordering is arbitrary even when the source looked like a list.
calls.ret: A new array holding the values.

namespaces.name: Ess.TextConsole
namespaces.doc: A typed-input console, no .gfx asset needed

calls.doc: Closes the text console, stops its polling loop, hides the widget and gives the player their controls back if they were locked.
calls.gotcha: Returns immediately when the console is not open, so calling it defensively is free.

calls.doc: Whether the text console is currently accepting input. Use it to avoid stacking a second prompt on top of a live one.

Opens the plain text-entry console - a prompt line the player types into, needing no .gfx asset. opts takes text (initial buffer), prompt (default "> "), max (default 200), lockPlayer (default true) and the onSubmit / onCancel / onChange callbacks. Buffered key events are drained first so the key that opened it does not leak into the buffer.
calls.gotcha: Enter fires onSubmit and clears the buffer but leaves the console OPEN; only Escape or Ess.TextConsole.close actually closes it. With lockPlayer left at its default the player cannot move until then.

namespaces.name: Ess.Time
namespaces.doc: All wall-clock timing (survives world-pause)

calls.doc: Returns a clock object with a :delta() method, an auto-advancing per-frame timer. maxDelta defaults to 0.25 seconds.
calls.gotcha: Auto-advancing: :delta() returns the time since its OWN last :delta() call and clamps it (default 0.25s), so a long pause or hitch can't blow up per-tick math. Don't mix it with the explicit stamp/elapsed flavour -- elapsed() never advances on its own, which is what makes a cooldown check idempotent.

calls.doc: Returns a ready() function that is true (and re-marks) at most once per seconds window, false otherwise without re-marking so a retry doesn't push the window back. The first call is always ready.
Returns seconds since the stamp was marked (Sys.TimeStampGetElapsed), or 0. since() is a plain alias for the same function.
Formats a raw seconds value (e.g. from elapsed()) into a HUD-ready display string via Junk.FormatTime.
pausable/scaled-clock mark
Re-marks an existing stamp handle in place (Sys.TimeStampMark). Every confirmed call site re-marks a stamp previously produced by stamp()/mainStamp() rather than creating a new one each time.
Convenience for scale(1) — undoes slow-motion under a clearer name.
Sets the world time scale via Sys.SetTimeScale(n) — confirmed idiom for slow-motion, e.g. Ess.Time.scale(0.2) for a 5x slowdown.
alias of elapsed (reads better at some call sites)
Creates a real-world time stamp via Sys.RealTimeStamp (pcall-guarded). Keeps advancing through world-pause and slow-motion, unlike mainStamp().
calls.gotcha: The REAL-WORLD clock -- it survives world-pause (menus/PDA), unlike Event.TimerRelative's own delta. Use Ess.Time.mainStamp for a gameplay cooldown that should freeze with the game.

namespaces.name: Ess.Track
namespaces.doc: One registry for every leak-prone Add/Remove pair

calls.doc: :add(closeFn) -> closeFn -- generic escape hatch: register any zero-arg teardown function.
register ANY of the five with a tracker, torn down by :closeAll()
:closeAll() -- runs every registered teardown in reverse-registration order, then clears the tracker.
:contextAction(uGuid, sLabelOrKey, ...) -> uGuid -- tracks Pg.AddContextAction for RemoveContextAction on teardown.
:disposer(uGuid, sCategory) -> uGuid -- tracks Object.AddToDisposer for RemoveFromDisposer on teardown.
:event(handle) -> handle -- tracks an Event.Create handle for Event.Delete on teardown.
:guid(uGuid) -> uGuid -- tracks a spawned object for Object.Remove on teardown.
:marker(handle) -> handle -- tracks a Marker.Add*() handle for Marker.Remove on teardown.

Creates a new tracker object; each :xxx() method on it both registers a teardown for that thing and returns the value you gave it, so you can wrap a spawn/creation call inline without an extra local variable.
calls.gotcha: Every Add.../Remove... pair on this engine is leak-prone: the handle is only accepted by its own matching Remove call, and there is NO clear-all native for ANY of them (Event, Marker, radar/PDA blips, quality refs, disposers, context actions). Register handles here at creation time, not at teardown time.

calls.doc: :pda(sName) -> sName -- tracks a Pda.Map:AddBlip({sName=...}) registration for RemoveBlip on teardown.
:qualityRef(uGuid, nQuality) -> ref -- tracks Object.AddQualityRef for RemoveQualityRef on teardown.
:radar(sName) -> sName -- tracks a Hud.Radar:AddObjective({sName=...}) registration for RemoveObjective on teardown.

namespaces.name: Ess.Triggers
namespaces.doc: .arm(spec, onFire, tracker) (stateless); .scope() → an isolated :arm/:armNamed/:gate/:declare/:markFired namespace

calls.doc: Passthrough to Ess.Raw.Triggers.arm; stays a bare top-level call because it's stateless and never names or shares state.

Returns an isolated named-trigger/gate namespace with its own private known/fired id tables, so two independent scopes can't collide even if they reuse the same ids. Ess.Contract gives each running contract instance its own scope.
calls.gotcha: Named trigger ids and gate inputs cross-reference BY NAME, so a single shared registry lets two unrelated systems both using an id like "start" silently satisfy each other's gates. Take your own scope per independent group of triggers -- the collision is then impossible by construction.

namespaces.name: Ess.UI
namespaces.doc: The 9-widget kit (native port of uilib)

calls.doc: Builds a labelled progress bar - health, a capture timer, a download meter. opts takes x/y/w/h, label and value.
calls.gotcha: :set takes a FRACTION from 0 to 1, not a percentage, and clamps - passing 50 pins the bar at full.
calls.ret: The bar object: :set(v), :label(s), plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.

calls.doc: Builds the two-pane browse board: a scrolling item list on the left and a detail pane on the right, fed by :detail{ category, rewards, objectives, progress, progressText }. Built for contract browsing but reusable for any list-plus-details screen. opts takes x/y/w/h, title, hint, items, detail, empty, focus and the onSelect / onChoose / onBack callbacks.
calls.gotcha: Unlike Ess.UI.List, the selection does NOT wrap at the ends, and both :items() and :select() fire onSelect immediately as a side effect.
calls.ret: The board object: :items(t), :selected() -> item, index, :select(i), :detail(d), :title(s), :hint(s), plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.

calls.doc: Builds the chat/log widget: a scrolling message area showing the last five wrapped lines, plus an optional typed input line. opts takes x/y/w/h, title, max (backlog, default 60), autoHide (seconds) and onSubmit.
calls.gotcha: opts.autoHide only starts counting after a :push, so an idle box with no messages never fades. The widget resizes itself to the number of visible lines, capped at five however large the backlog is.
calls.ret: The chat object: :push(text), :prompt(onSubmit), :clear(), :title(s), plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.

calls.doc: Shows the modal yes/no prompt and calls opts.onResult(true or false) with the answer. opts takes title, text, yes, no and onResult; focus is restored to whatever held it when the prompt resolves.
calls.gotcha: One shared instance serves the whole framework - opening a second Confirm overwrites the first's callback, which is then never called. The highlight starts on NO, and Escape resolves as false.

calls.doc: Gives one widget exclusive keyboard focus. Also swallows any buffered key events (so the keypress that triggered the change does not leak into the newly focused widget) and wakes the UI heartbeat.
calls.gotcha: Exactly one widget hears keys at a time - focusing a new one silently takes focus away from whatever had it, with no notification to the old holder.

calls.doc: The widget currently holding keyboard focus.
calls.ret: The focused widget object, or nil when nothing has focus.

calls.doc: Shows the modal single-line text prompt: Enter fires opts.onSubmit(text), Escape fires opts.onCancel, and focus returns to whatever held it before. opts takes prompt, text (initial value), max (default 120), onSubmit and onCancel.
calls.gotcha: One shared instance for the whole framework, so a second Input replaces the first's callbacks. Only characters Ess.Input.VkToChar can map are accepted, which means a US keyboard layout.

calls.doc: Builds the scrolling, keyboard-driven selection list widget. opts takes x/y/w/h, title, crumb, hint, items, empty (the text shown for an empty list), focus, and the onChoose / onBack / onSelect callbacks. Each item is a table with a `label`, or a `header` for a non-selectable section caption.
calls.gotcha: Shows 10 rows at a time and WRAPS at both ends - pressing down on the last row jumps to the first. Header entries are skipped by every move and can never become the selection.
calls.ret: The list object: :items(t), :selected() -> item, index, :select(i), :title/:crumb/:hint, plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.

calls.doc: Declarative drill-down menu constructor (ForgeMenu-style). Options: title, id (defaults to title), key (toggle key, display only), x/y (default 40, 60), onClose.
Builds a simple text panel of up to eight lines - the readout widget for a stats display or a dev overlay. opts takes x/y/w/h, title and lines.
calls.gotcha: Lines are indexed 0..7, not 1..8. Writing a non-blank line auto-grows the panel to fit, but it never shrinks on its own - call :fit or :clear to pull it back in.
calls.ret: The panel object: :title(s), :line(i, s), :fit(n), :clear(), plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.

calls.doc: Pops a short, self-expiring notification in the corner of the screen. Text is word-wrapped to two lines, and the toast claims a free slot or, if all are busy, the one expiring soonest. opts takes ttl (seconds, default Ess.UI.TOAST_TTL).
calls.gotcha: Only Ess.UI.TOAST_SLOTS (3 by default) toasts exist, so a burst of messages overwrites itself. Anything past the second wrapped line is dropped without a hint.
calls.ret: The toast object, which offers :dismiss() to clear it early.

calls.doc: ============================ widget-common ============================= show/hide/focus/blur/destroy shared by every widget object.

Internal: arms the single shared Ess.UI heartbeat if it is not already running. Deliberately guarded by isRunning rather than calling Ess.Loop.start unconditionally, because start() reschedules a live loop and would keep pushing the next tick back on every :show().
calls.gotcha: The tick returns needsTick(), so the heartbeat STOPS ITSELF as soon as nothing needs servicing. Anything that creates new work (a new toast, a size change, a focus grab) has to call this again to wake it back up.

calls.doc: Internal: adds a widget to the engine's live list so the shared heartbeat services it - warmup repaints after the async movie load, size easing, and auto-hide countdowns. Every Ess.UI constructor calls it; it is idempotent, so a repeat registration is ignored.
body-resize easing target (the "Forge feel"); waking the heartbeat animates it
Formats a number with thousands separators - 1234567 becomes "1,234,567" - for cash, score and ammo readouts.
calls.gotcha: Floors to an integer first, so any fractional part is dropped rather than rounded, and a non-number argument silently becomes 0.

calls.doc: Formats a count of seconds as M:SS for a countdown or elapsed-time readout.
calls.gotcha: Minutes never roll over into hours and are never zero-padded, so 3700 seconds reads "61:40".

calls.doc: Maps a virtual-key code to the semantic navigation direction it means, reading the remappable Ess.UI.KEYS table. Every Ess.UI widget's key handler starts with this call, which is why rebinding Ess.UI.KEYS.up retargets the whole kit at once.
calls.ret: One of "up", "down", "left", "right", "enter", "esc" - or nil for any other key.

namespaces.name: Ess.Vec
namespaces.doc: 3D vector math on flat x,y,z (aim / offset / knockback)

calls.sig: Ess.Vec.add(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)
calls.doc: Ess.Vec.sub(a, b) -> x,y,z   (a - b, i.e. the vector b->a)

calls.sig: Ess.Vec.cross(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz)
calls.doc: V.cross(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz) -> cx, cy, cz -- the cross product (the perpendicular): dot's missing sibling.

calls.sig: Ess.Vec.dir(fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz)
calls.doc: Unit direction from A to B (normalize(sub(B, A))).

calls.sig: Ess.Vec.dot(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)
calls.doc: Dot product of two 3D vectors. With unit directions, the sign answers "are these two roughly pointing the same way" - positive means yes, negative means opposed, zero means perpendicular.
Magnitude of a 3D vector given as three loose components - how long a direction/velocity/offset is.
calls.ret: The length as a single number.

calls.sig: Ess.Vec.lerp(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2, t)
calls.doc: Interpolates between two positions. Powers Ess.Easy.Camera's follow-damping (via per-tick easing rather than snapping), confirmed working live in that consumer even though Ess.Vec itself is only offline-verified.
Unit vector of (x,y,z); a zero-length input returns 0,0,0 rather than NaN.
Multiplies each component of a vector by s. The usual way to turn a unit direction into a shove of a given strength before feeding it to Ess.Object.impulse.
calls.gotcha: Returns three separate values, so it expands fully only as the LAST argument of a call. Nesting it inside another Vec call passes just x - capture into locals first.
calls.ret: Three values: the scaled x, y, z.

calls.sig: Ess.Vec.sub(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)
calls.doc: Component-wise subtraction of the second point from the first, giving the vector that points from point 2 to point 1.
calls.gotcha: Same multi-return caveat as the rest of Ess.Vec - it only expands in full as the last argument of a call.
calls.ret: Three values: the difference x, y, z.

calls.sig: Ess.Vec.toward(fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz, dist)
calls.doc: The point dist units from A toward B.

namespaces.name: Ess.Vehicle
namespaces.doc: Seats/riders/entry/upkeep

calls.doc: The character currently in the driver's seat of a vehicle. AI orders must target the driver, not the hull, so this is how you get a usable actor guid out of a vehicle.
calls.ret: The driver's guid, or nil when the seat is empty or the read failed.

calls.doc: pcall-wrapped MrxUtil.EnterBestAvailableSeat — confirmed driver/gunner/passenger/cargo seat priority order.
calls.gotcha: Flagged caution (unconfirmed causally but repeatable enough to record): immediately after a Pg.Spawn + enterBestSeat from INSIDE an interior cell, the very next bridge chunk -- even a bare `return 1+1` -- stalled the Lua tick for 30+ seconds with the process still alive, recoverable only by killing the game. Avoid spawning and entering a vehicle from inside an interior.

calls.doc: Puts a character into the best free seat of a vehicle while refusing the seat types you list. Tries driver, gunner, passenger, cargo in that order ("d", "g", "p", "c") and takes the first one it can actually board - the way to load passengers without letting them steal the wheel.
calls.ret: true plus the seat-type letter that was taken, or false, nil when every allowed seat failed.

calls.doc: force EVERY occupant out (Ai.EveryoneOut)
Confirmed signature+usage from DestroyerTool.lua: calls Vehicle.Exit(uVehicle, uCharacter, true).

Sends an AI helicopter to a world point via Ai.Deliver(driver, x, y, z, dropHeight, careless) — not Ai.Goal "MoveToPos", which does not fly a heli. Since a freshly-spawned heli has no driver for a moment, this polls Ess.Vehicle.driver until one exists before issuing the order. opts.height (default 0.5), opts.careless, opts.onReady(driver) fire once the order is issued; returns cancel() to stop the driver-wait early.

Spawns a template and returns a ghost object (ghost.guid, ghost:update(nx,ny,nz), ghost:remove()). Object.SetPosition silently fails to move a spawned human, so update() tries SetPosition then re-reads the real position; if still off by more than ~3 units it despawns/respawns the template instead, updating ghost.guid so callers always read the current handle.
Vehicle.IsFlipped, live-confirmed boolean (2026-07-22).
command an AI heli to descend (Ai.HeliLand)
fly a crewed heli a few laps around a point (the "victory lap" flight); opts.radius/height/orbits/...
full heal + rearm (RestoreHealth/RestoreAmmo)
Everyone currently aboard a vehicle, driver and passengers alike.
calls.gotcha: An empty table also means "the read failed", so a zero length does not prove the vehicle is really empty.
calls.ret: An array of character guids - empty when there is nobody, never nil.

calls.doc: Returns which seat a character currently occupies, if any. Together with driver/riders this collapses a 7-getter native overlap down to the 3 shapes actually needed day to day.
